summary: Two judges in Yerushalayim, Admon and Chanan, made rulings. Chanan says a woman whose husband went far away swears only at the end, when she collects her kesubah; the sons of the Kohanim Gedolim say she swears at the beginning too.

chunks.en: There were two judges of decrees in Yerushalayim:
chunks.st: There were two prominent judges who issued decrees in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: Admon and Chanan ben Avishalom.
chunks.st: Admon and Ḥanan ben Avishalom. Ḥanan

chunks.en: Chanan says two things,
chunks.st: states two matters about which the Sages disagreed;

chunks.en: Admon says seven.
chunks.st: Admon states seven.

chunks.en: One who went away across the sea
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: With regard to the case of one who went overseas

chunks.en: and his wife asks for food,
chunks.st: and his wife is demanding sustenance, claiming that her husband left her without funds and she is seeking a ruling that would provide for her from her husband’s property, Ḥ

chunks.en: Chanan says,
chunks.st: anan says:

chunks.en: she swears at the end, and does not swear at the beginning.
chunks.explain: She swears he did not leave her money.
chunks.st: She takes an oath at the end of their marriage, i.e., when she learns that her husband died. The oath is to the effect that he did not leave her any funds when he departed overseas, as she is claiming full payment of her marriage contract. And she does not take an oath at the outset
chunks.stMore: of his trip overseas, when she demands support soon after his departure.

chunks.he: נֶחְלְקוּ עָלָיו בְּנֵי כֹהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים וְאָמְרוּ,
chunks.en: The sons of the Kohanim Gedolim argued with him and said,
chunks.st: The sons of High Priests disagreed with Ḥanan’s opinion and said:

chunks.en: she swears at the beginning and at the end.
chunks.st: She takes an oath both at the outset and at the end.

chunks.he: אָמַר רַבִּי דוֹסָא בֶן הַרְכִּינָס כְּדִבְרֵיהֶם.
chunks.en: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said like their words.
chunks.st: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said: The halakha is in accordance with their statement, i.e., that of the sons of the High Priests.

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said,
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said that Ḥ

chunks.en: Chanan said it well:
chunks.st: anan spoke well:

chunks.en: she swears only at the end.
chunks.st: She takes an oath only at the end.

summary: Someone fed the wife of a man who was away across the sea, and now wants his money back. Chanan says he lost his money, but the sons of the Kohanim Gedolim say he swears how much he spent and takes it.
stIntro: In the case of a husband

chunks.en: One who went away across the sea, and someone
chunks.st: who went overseas, and someone arose

chunks.en: came and supported his wife,
chunks.st: and sustained his wife in his absence, and upon the husband’s return the provider demands from him the money he spent on his wife, Ḥ

chunks.en: Chanan says,
chunks.st: anan says:

chunks.en: he lost his money.
chunks.st: He has lost his money,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the husband is not obligated to repay him, as the provider acted of his own free will and was not instructed to do so by the husband.

chunks.he: נֶחְלְקוּ עָלָיו בְּנֵי כֹהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים וְאָמְרוּ,
chunks.en: The sons of the Kohanim Gedolim argued with him and said,
chunks.st: The sons of High Priests disagreed with Ḥanan’s opinion and said:

chunks.en: he swears how much he spent, and takes it.
chunks.st: The man swears how much he spent on behalf of the woman, and he takes that sum from the husband.

chunks.he: אָמַר רַבִּי דוֹסָא בֶן הַרְכִּינָס כְּדִבְרֵיהֶם.
chunks.en: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said like their words.
chunks.st: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said that the halakha is in accordance with their statement.

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said: Ḥ

chunks.en: Chanan said it well:
chunks.st: anan spoke well

chunks.en: he put his money on the horn of a deer.
chunks.explain: He cannot expect to get it back.
chunks.st: in this case, as this man is like one who placed his money on the horn of a deer
chunks.stMore: in midflight, i.e., he has no reasonable expectation of reimbursement.

summary: Admon disagrees in seven cases. When there is little money left after a man dies, the daughters are fed and the sons get nothing, and Admon asks, Should I lose because I am a boy?

chunks.en: Admon says seven.
chunks.st: Admon states a dissenting opinion to that of the Rabbis in seven cases.

chunks.en: One who died and left sons and daughters:
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: With regard to one who died and left behind both sons and daughters,

chunks.en: when there is a lot of property,
chunks.st: when the estate is large

chunks.en: the sons inherit and the daughters are fed.
chunks.st: the sons inherit the property and the daughters are provided with sustenance from it.

chunks.en: And when there is little property,
chunks.st: And with regard to a small estate,
chunks.stMore: which is insufficient to provide for both the sons and the daughters,

chunks.he: הַבָּנוֹת יִזּוֹנוּ וְהַבָּנִים יְחַזְּרוּ עַל הַפְּתָחִים.
chunks.en: the daughters are fed and the sons go around to the doors.
chunks.explain: They have to ask people for help.
chunks.st: the daughters are provided with sustenance and the sons have neither inheritance nor sustenance, and therefore, if they have no other means with which to support themselves, they must go round begging at the doors.

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says:

chunks.en: Because I am a boy, should I lose?
chunks.st: Because I am a male, will I lose out?

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: I agree with what Admon says.
chunks.st: I see as correct the statement of Admon.

summary: One person says another owes him jugs of oil, and the other admits he owes only the empty jugs. Admon says he must swear, the Sages say not, and Rabban Gamliel agrees with Admon.
stIntro: The mishna cites another case involving a dispute between Admon and the Rabbis. With regard to

chunks.en: One who claims his friend owes him jugs of oil,
chunks.st: one who claims that another owes him jugs of oil,

chunks.en: and the friend admits to the empty jugs,
chunks.st: and the other admits to the claim of pitchers but not the oil,

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says:

chunks.en: since he admitted part of the claim,
chunks.st: Since he made a partial admission to the claim,

chunks.en: he must swear. But the Sages say,
chunks.st: he takes an oath swearing that he owes only what he has admitted to and no more. And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: this is not admitting to the same kind of thing as the claim.
chunks.st: The partial admission in this case is not of the same type as the claim,
chunks.stMore: as the claim specified oil and the admission referred to pitchers.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: I agree with what Admon says.
chunks.st: I see as correct the statement of Admon.

summary: A father promised money to his daughter's chasan and then lost all his money. Admon says the kallah can tell the chasan to marry her or let her go, and Rabban Gamliel agrees.
stIntro: The mishna states another case involving a ruling of Admon. With regard to one who promises and

chunks.en: One who promised money to his son-in-law and then
chunks.st: apportions money for his son-in-law as a dowry, and he

chunks.en: lost all his money,
chunks.explain: Like stretching out your foot to say, I have nothing.
chunks.st: went bankrupt,
chunks.stMore: and he now claims that he does not have the money to fulfill his financial obligations,

chunks.en: she may sit and wait until her hair turns white.
chunks.st: the betrothed woman can be left to sit unwed in her father’s house until her head turns white.
chunks.stMore: If the groom does not wish to marry without a dowry he cannot be forced to do so, as the father failed to fulfill his promise.

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says that

chunks.en: she can say,
chunks.st: she can say:

chunks.en: If I had promised it myself,
chunks.st: Had I apportioned the money myself

chunks.en: I would sit until my hair turns white.
chunks.st: and broken my promise, I would agree to sit until my head turns white.

chunks.en: But now that my father promised for me,
chunks.st: However, now that my father was the one who apportioned the dowry,

chunks.en: what can I do?
chunks.st: what can I do?

chunks.en: Either marry me or let me go.
chunks.st: Either marry me or release me by a bill of divorce.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: I agree with what Admon says.
chunks.st: I see as correct the statement of Admon.

summary: A man says a field is his, but he signed as a witness when it was sold to someone else. Admon says he can still claim it, and the Sages say he lost his right.

chunks.en: One who claims a field is his, and he
chunks.st: one who contests ownership of a field, claiming that a field under the control of someone else actually belongs to him, and the claimant himself

chunks.en: signed on its sale as a witness,
chunks.st: is signed as a witness on the bill of sale to that other person,

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says:

chunks.en: he can say,
chunks.st: His signature does not disprove his claim of ownership of the property, as it is possible that the claimant said to himself:

chunks.he: הַשֵּׁנִי נֹחַ לִי וְהָרִאשׁוֹן קָשֶׁה הֵימֶנּוּ.
chunks.en: The second one is easy for me, and the first one is harder than him.
chunks.st: The second person is easier for me, as I can reason with him, but the first owner, who sold the field to the current holder, is more difficult to deal with than him.
chunks.stMore: The claimant might have been afraid to protest against the first one, who is perhaps violent, and therefore he was even willing to sign as a witness to transfer the field to the control of someone more amenable to his ensuing protest.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he lost his right.
chunks.st: He has lost his right
chunks.stMore: to contest ownership, as he signed a bill of sale that states that the field belongs to the present holder.

chunks.en: If he used it as a border marker for another field,
chunks.st: If he established that field as a marker for another field,

chunks.en: he lost his right.
chunks.st: everyone agrees that he has lost his right.
chunks.stMore: In other words, if the claimant wrote a document concerning another field and in that document he listed the first field as a boundary marker and described it as belonging to someone else, even Admon concedes that he has lost his right, as he had no reason to say it belonged to someone else other than his belief this was in fact the case.

summary: A man went far away and the path to his field was lost. Admon says he may walk the shortest way, and the Sages say he must buy a path even if it costs a lot.

chunks.en: One who went away across the sea,
chunks.st: one who went overseas and in the meantime

chunks.en: and the path to his field was lost,
chunks.st: the path leading to his field was lost,
chunks.stMore: e.g., the path he used to reach his land was taken over by the owner of the field through which it passed, so that its exact position is now unknown,

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says:

chunks.en: let him go the shortest way.
chunks.st: Let him go to his field by the shortest possible route.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: let him buy a path even for a hundred maneh,
chunks.st: Let him buy himself a path from an owner of a neighboring field at whatever price he can, even if it is one hundred maneh,

chunks.en: or fly through the air.
chunks.st: or let him fly through the air.

summary: A lender shows a loan document, and the borrower shows that the lender later sold him a field. Admon says the lender should have taken his money then, but the Sages say the lender was smart to sell it.

chunks.en: One who brings out a loan document against his friend,
chunks.st: one who produces a promissory note against another,

chunks.he: וְהַלָּה הוֹצִיא שֶׁמָּכַר לוֹ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה,
chunks.en: and the other brought out a paper that he sold him the field,
chunks.st: and this borrower produced a bill of sale dated after the promissory note that states that the lender sold him a field of his,

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says

chunks.en: he can say,
chunks.st: that the borrower can say:

chunks.en: If I really owed you,
chunks.st: Were I really indebted to you,

chunks.en: you should have collected what was yours
chunks.st: you should have collected your loan

chunks.en: when you sold me the field.
chunks.st: when you sold me the field, and you would not have needed to sell it.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: this one was smart, that he sold
chunks.st: This is no proof, as it is possible that this lender was perspicacious, as he sold

chunks.en: him the land,
chunks.st: the borrower the land for a good reason,

chunks.en: because now he can take it as a pledge.
chunks.st: because now he can take the field as collateral from him in lieu of the outstanding loan.

words.en: to take it as a pledge

summary: Two people each show a loan document against the other. Admon says the later document must be fake, and the Sages say each one collects his own loan.

chunks.en: Two people who brought out loan documents
chunks.st: two people who each produced a promissory note of a monetary debt

chunks.en: against each other.
chunks.st: against the other,

chunks.en: Admon says,
chunks.st: Admon says:
chunks.stMore: The one holding the note with the later date can say to the first:

chunks.en: If I owed you,
chunks.st: If I owed you money,

chunks.en: how could you borrow from me?
chunks.st: how is it that you are borrowing from me?
chunks.stMore: You should have sued to collect your debt. This is proof that your document is a forgery.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: this one collects his loan
chunks.st: This one collects his promissory note,

chunks.en: and that one collects his loan.
chunks.st: and that one collects his promissory note.

summary: For marriage, Eretz Yisrael has three lands: Yehudah, Ever HaYarden and the Galil. A husband cannot make his wife move from one land to another, or from a town to a city, but he may move her to a better place.

chunks.en: There are three lands for marriage:
chunks.st: three separate lands with regard to marriage:

chunks.en: Yehudah, Ever HaYarden,
chunks.st: Judea, Transjordan,

chunks.he: וְהַגָּלִיל. אֵין מוֹצִיאִין מֵעִיר לְעִיר וּמִכְּרַךְ לִכְרַךְ.
chunks.en: and the Galil. We do not move a wife from town to town or city to city in another land.
chunks.st: and the Galilee. If a man marries a woman in one of these lands he may not remove her from one town to another town in another of these lands or from one city to another city,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he cannot compel her to move to another land.

chunks.en: But in the same land,
chunks.st: However, in the same land

chunks.en: we may move her from town to town and city to city,
chunks.st: one may remove her from one town to another town or from one city to another city.

chunks.en: but not from a town to a city,
chunks.st: However, even within the same land one may not force his wife to move from a town to a city,

chunks.en: and not from a city to a town.
chunks.st: nor from a city to a town.

chunks.en: We may move her from a bad home to a nice home,
chunks.st: The mishna adds: One may remove his wife from a noxious residence to a pleasant residence, even if it is in another land.

chunks.he: אֲבָל לֹא מִנָּוֶה הַיָּפָה לְנָוֶה הָרָעָה.
chunks.en: but not from a nice home to a bad home.
chunks.st: However, one may not compel his wife to move from a pleasant residence to a noxious residence.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: אַף לֹא מִנָּוֶה רָעָה לְנָוֶה יָפָה,
chunks.en: not even from a bad home to a nice home,
chunks.st: One may also not remove her from a noxious residence to a pleasant residence,

chunks.en: because a nice home tests a person.
chunks.explain: A change, even a nice one, can be hard.
chunks.st: because a pleasant residence tests
chunks.stMore: the individual, i.e., one accustomed to certain environments can suffer even in more comfortable living quarters.

summary: A husband or wife can make the family move up to Eretz Yisrael and to Yerushalayim, but not leave them. The mishnah also teaches which money a kesubah is paid in.

chunks.en: Anyone can make the family move up to Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: All may force their family to ascend to Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one may compel his family and household to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: but no one can make them leave.
chunks.st: but all may not remove
chunks.stMore: others from Eretz Yisrael, as one may not coerce one’s family to leave.

chunks.en: Anyone can make them move up to Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: Likewise, all may force their family to ascend to Jerusalem,

chunks.en: but no one can make them leave,
chunks.st: and all may not, i.e., no one may, remove them from Jerusalem.

chunks.en: both men and women (and slaves).
chunks.st: Both men and women
chunks.stMore: may force the other spouse to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael or to move to Jerusalem. The mishna lists other halakhic distinctions between various geographic locations: If one

chunks.en: If he married a woman in Eretz Yisrael
chunks.st: married a woman in Eretz Yisrael

chunks.en: and divorced her in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: and divorced her in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.stMore: and the currency of the sum in the marriage contract was not specified,

chunks.en: he gives her in the money of Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: he gives her the sum of her marriage contract in the currency of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.he: נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה בְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגֵרְשָׁהּ בְּקַפּוֹטְקִיָּא,
chunks.en: If he married a woman in Eretz Yisrael and divorced her in Kapotkiya,
chunks.st: If one married a woman in Eretz Yisrael and divorced her in Cappadocia, where the currency holds greater value,

words.note: A land far away, where the coins were worth more.

chunks.en: he gives her in the money of Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: he gives her the currency of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.he: נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה בְקַפּוֹטְקִיָּא וְגֵרְשָׁהּ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: If he married a woman in Kapotkiya and divorced her in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: If one married a woman in Cappadocia and divorced her in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: he gives her in the money of Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: he likewise gives her the currency of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: he gives her in the money of Kapotkiya.
chunks.st: He gives her the currency of Cappadocia.

chunks.en: If he married a woman in Kapotkiya and divorced her in Kapotkiya,
chunks.st: Everyone agrees that if one married a woman in Cappadocia and divorced her in Cappadocia,

chunks.en: he gives her in the money of Kapotkiya.
chunks.st: he gives her the currency of Cappadocia.
